title: Iguana configuration
description: Settings for the Iguana window manager. Every setting is optional.

gaps.description: Empty space around and between tiled windows, in points.

outer.description: Space between the windows and the edge of the screen. One number for all sides, or a table with top, left, bottom and right.

auto-split.description: A new window splits the focused window along its longer side. When false it is added to the focused window's row or column.

resize-step.description: Share of the container that one resize step moves (0.05 is five percent).

stack-peek.description: Points of each window in a stack that stay visible behind the window in front.

mouse-follows-focus.description: Move the pointer to the centre of a window when a shortcut focuses it.

focus-follows-mouse.description: Focus the window the pointer comes to rest on, without a click.

animation.description: How windows travel to their new place. Switched off automatically while Reduce Motion is on.

enabled.description: Windows glide to their new place instead of jumping.

duration.description: Seconds a window takes to reach its new place.

focus-ring.description: A ring around the window that has the focus, tiled or floating. It is drawn just outside the window and never covers its content.

enabled.description: Draw a ring around the focused window.

width.description: Thickness of the ring, in points.

color.description: "accent" follows the accent colour chosen in System Settings. Or a colour of your own: "#rgb", "#rrggbb", or "#rrggbbaa" with an opacity.

reserve-strip.description: Room for Stage Manager's strip of recent apps: "auto" leaves room while the strip is shown, false tiles underneath it, a number reserves that many points.

strip-width.description: Width used when reserve-strip is "auto" or true.

desktops.description: Which desktops the menu bar icon draws: the one you are on, every desktop side by side, or every desktop that has windows.

click-to-switch.description: With more than one desktop drawn, a click on one of them goes to it instead of opening the menu.

updates.description: Noticing a newer Iguana. Nothing is ever downloaded or installed.

check.description: About once a day, ask GitHub whether a newer version has been released, and say so in the menu of the menu bar item. The request carries nothing about you or this Mac.

hooks.description: Shell commands Iguana runs when something changes, for status bars and scripts. Each is run with /bin/sh -c and gets the facts in environment variables: IGUANA_EVENT, IGUANA_DESKTOP, IGUANA_DISPLAY and, for the focus, IGUANA_WINDOW_ID, IGUANA_APP and IGUANA_TITLE.

desktop-changed.description: Run when the desktop a display is showing changed. An empty string runs nothing.

focus-changed.description: Run when a different window has the focus. An empty string runs nothing. In a script, write "$IGUANA_TITLE" with the quotes: a window title can be any text.

bindings.description: Keyboard shortcuts. The key is modifiers and a key joined by dashes, the value is a command. Leave a shortcut out to keep its built-in command, or set it to "" to switch it off.

^((cmd|command|super|ctrl|control|opt|op.description: A command, for example "focus left" or "move-to-space 3 --stay".

rule.description: Windows that should stay floating, or be sent to a desktop or a display when they first appear. Written as [[rule]] sections. The first rule that matches a window decides.

app.description: A bundle identifier (exact match) or part of the app's name.

title.description: A regular expression matched against the window title, ignoring case.

float.description: Whether matching windows float. A rule with none of float, desktop and display floats them; a rule with only desktop or display leaves floating alone.

desktop.description: Send a matching window to this desktop when it first appears, and stay on the desktop being used. Desktops are numbered as Mission Control numbers them.

display.description: Send a matching window to this display when it first appears, onto the desktop the display is showing, and stay where you are. Part of the display's name, ignoring case, or the display's number: displays are numbered from 1, left to right. A rule that has desktop does not use display.
